title: RelativeErrorSmoothConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable convex minimization of f:E→ℝ. The objective satisfies the global quadratic smoothness inequality with public L>0 and has a minimizer xstar satisfying ‖x0−xstar‖≤R, where R≥0 is public.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: A query x∈E returns g∈E satisfying ‖g−∇f(x)‖≤α‖∇f(x)‖ for every call index and seed. Only gradient information is supplied; function values are unavailable. The public error parameter satisfies 0≤α<1.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: Arbitrary bias and dependence between oracle calls are permitted; no unbiasedness, independence, or distributional noise restriction is imposed beyond the uniform relative-error bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: relative_error
distinctive_assumptions.details: The error bound is pointwise relative to the true gradient norm, uniformly over all x, call indices k, and seeds. Errors vanish at stationary points.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary real Hilbert space, with no finite-dimensional restriction. E, x0, L, α, R, and ε are public because Params=Public and publicInput is the identity; f and its minimizer are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: Gradient.Public; LongTails/Setups/RelativeErrorSmoothConvex.lean: Public, spec.Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return one point output∈E satisfying f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar, with public ε>0.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law. The oracle-call budget is fixed and must hold for every seed.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth convex minimization is classical, but this formulation uses a uniformly bounded relative-error gradient oracle permitting arbitrary bias and dependence, with an almost-sure guarantee in an arbitrary Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Relative Error

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. The function admits a quadratic upper model with curvature L>0, and a given starting point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At x, the oracle returns a vector g satisfying ∥g−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥, where 0≤α<1. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The algorithm receives E, L, x0, α, R, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For every x,y∈E, f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩≤f(y),f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 3 (Relative oracle error). Queries may be made at any point of E. For every finite query–reply history h, every query x∈E, and every realization s of the oracle randomness used for that reply, the returned vector g(h,x,s)∈E satisfies ∥g(h,x,s)−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥. Oracle randomness may be dependent across calls, and replies may depend on the history. The algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle randomness.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Convex differentiable f on a real Hilbert space satisfies f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2, with L>0, a minimizer x⋆, and ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, R≥0. Every oracle reply satisfies ∥g−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥, 0≤α<1, for every call and seed. Target: f(xN)−f(x⋆)≤ε, ε>0, almost surely under the execution measure (indeed, for every seed). Parameters L,α,R,ε are supplied.

(2) Regularized RE-AGM (Vasin and Gasnikov 2026, Thm. 7.2) O((T+αT)(1+log⁡T)). T>1, α≤1/3; Euclidean space. (1): α2T instead of αT; removes logarithm on T>1, α≤1/3. At α=T−1/4, T≥81: O(T3/4(1+log⁡T))→O(T). Scope: every α<1.
(3) Regularized GD (Vasin and Gasnikov 2026, Thm. 7.1) O((1+α)2(1−α)6T(1+log⁡T)). T>1, α<1/2; Euclidean space. (1): O(T+α2T) on T>1, α<1/2; logarithmic saving throughout. For α≤T−1/4: O(T(1+log⁡T))→O(T). Scope: every α<1.
(4) ISTM, p=2 (Kornilov et al. 2023, Thm. 3.1) O(1+T) when α≤cmin{1,T−1/2}; Euclidean space. Certified accuracy floor of order α2LR2. (1): matches O(T) for T>1, α≲T−1/2; extends acceleration to α≲T−1/4 with α≤1/3. Arbitrary accuracy for every α<1.

Abbr: T=LR2/ε; complexity counts relative-error gradient calls; c>0 is a sufficiently small universal constant; ≲ suppresses a universal constant. GD: gradient descent; RE-AGM: relative-error accelerated gradient method; ISTM: intermediate similar triangle method.

import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.RelativeErrorSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public extends toGradientPublic : LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.Public where
  α : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := fun p => p
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.α ∧ p.α < 1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f oracle :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ ≤ f y) ∧
    (∀ x y, f y ≤ f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ + p.L / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed - gradient f x‖ ≤ p.α * ‖gradient f x‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R)
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.RelativeErrorSmoothConvex
